title: Uniform mixing and $ε$-uniform mixing on cycles
abstract: We study continuous-time quantum walks on cycles. We prove two complementary results. Firstly, the cycle $C_9$ does not admit uniform mixing at any time. Using the similar idea and Dickson polynomials, we prove that $C_{15}$ does not admit uniform mixing at any time neither. Secondly, for every prime $p$, we show that the cycle $C_{p^2}$ admits $ε$-uniform mixing.
summary: This paper mathematically analyzes the mixing behavior of continuous-time quantum walks on cycle graphs. It establishes that certain cycles, such as $C_9$ and $C_{15}$, fail to achieve perfect uniform mixing at any time. Conversely, it proves a positive result by showing that for all prime powers $p^2$, the walk achieves $\epsilon$-uniform mixing.
main_problem: The study investigates the conditions under which continuous-time quantum walks on cycle graphs exhibit uniform or $\epsilon$-uniform mixing.
main_result: The paper proves that $C_9$ and $C_{15}$ never achieve uniform mixing, while demonstrating that for every prime $p$, the cycle $C_{p^2}$ does admit $\epsilon$-uniform mixing.
method: The analysis combines spectral graph theory (using eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix) with advanced algebraic techniques like solving polynomial systems via Gröbner bases to derive necessary conditions for mixing.
model_or_system: The model is a continuous-time quantum walk evolving on a cycle graph $C_n$, governed by the unitary evolution operator $U(t) = \exp(itA)$, where $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $C_n$.
key_observables: Uniform mixing (requiring $|U(t)_{u,v}|^2 = 1/n$) and $\epsilon$-uniform mixing ($\|U(t) \circ U(t)^{*−1} - nJ\| < \epsilon$).
important_parameters: The cycle length $n$ (specifically $C_9$, $C_{15}$, and $C_{p^2}$), the time $t$, and the error tolerance $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on properties derived from circulant matrices and algebraic number theory related to roots of unity.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing general conditions for uniform mixing using spectral properties, then applying these methods via Gröbner basis computations to disprove mixing for $C_9$ and $C_{15}$, concluding with a constructive proof of $\epsilon$-uniform mixing for $C_{p^2}$.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical analysis connecting graph structure (cycles) to quantum dynamical properties like mixing rates is highly relevant for understanding decoherence or thermalization in open quantum systems.
